key_insight: Steeper interfacial mechanical-property gradients produce greater crack-tip field asymmetry and deflect crack growth toward softer SA387 in SA387–Alloy 82–316L welded joints.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for spatially varying weld properties can improve crack-path prediction and structural integrity assessment of dissimilar metal joints.
method: Characterized weld interfaces using microstructural observations and Vickers hardness measurements.
Implemented location-dependent mechanical properties in ABAQUS using the USDFLD subroutine.
Examined crack-tip stress, strain, stress triaxiality, and crack-growth paths.
evidence_signal: Measurements identified a steep SA387/82 property gradient and a smoother 82/316L transition, while simulations showed stronger crack-tip asymmetry and deflection at the steeper interface.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative crack-path prediction error or independent experimental validation of simulated crack growth.
paper_title: Characterization of Interfacial Mechanical Heterogeneity and Prediction of Crack Growth Path in Heterogeneous Welded Joints
